back2basics.text: Energy transition refers to shifting from fossil fuels like coal, oil, and gas to cleaner energy sources such as solar and wind to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Climate justice focuses on fair treatment and support for countries and communities most affected by climate change, ensuring they receive adequate finance and protection while global emissions are reduced.

2026-11-11-pm-14182d1a45.deck: At COP31 in Antalya, countries focused on accelerating the shift from fossil fuels to clean energy and addressing climate justice through global cooperation and finance. This summit is crucial for understanding evolving international climate policies and India's engagement in sustainable development.

editor.mainsAngle: Feeds into environment conservation, climate change policies, and India's role in global climate governance.
editor.prelimsAngle: COP31 is a UN climate conference focusing on energy transition beyond fossil fuels.
editor.why: COP31 sets global climate policies impacting energy transition, sustainable development, and international cooperation relevant to environment and economy.

faq.a: To increase electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35% by 2035.

faq.a: It is a voluntary roadmap to help countries plan the transition away from fossil fuels.
faq.q: What is the nature of Brazil’s energy transition roadmap presented at COP31?

faq.a: To generate funds for climate finance supporting vulnerable countries and to enforce the polluter pays principle.
faq.q: Why did the UN Secretary-General call for taxing fossil fuel companies at COP31?

body: Discuss COP31’s focus on fossil fuel phase-out, electrification, and infrastructure challenges.
Examine the climate justice compact proposed by the UN Secretary-General and the emphasis on polluter pays principle.
Analyse participation dynamics, including India’s initiatives and attendance of global leaders.
Evaluate unresolved issues such as climate finance, loss and damage, and just transition mechanisms.
structure.conclusion: COP31 advances dialogue and initiatives but faces challenges in implementation and global cooperation.
structure.intro: International climate summits provide a platform for countries to negotiate and coordinate actions on climate change.

mcq.stem: Consider the following statements about COP31: 1. Türkiye’s 35-by-35 initiative aims to increase electricity’s share in global energy consumption to 35% by 2035. 2. Brazil’s roadmap for energy transition is a binding international agreement to phase out fossil fuels.
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because Brazil’s roadmap is voluntary and not a binding agreement.

body.label: Fossil fuel phase-out roadmap
body.text: Brazil presented a voluntary roadmap to help countries transition away from fossil fuels by creating national plans that address demand, production, and economic impacts.

body.label: Electrification goals
body.text: Türkiye promoted its '35-by-35' initiative aiming to increase electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35% by 2035, focusing on electrifying transport, buildings, and industry.

body.label: Grid infrastructure challenges
body.text: A major barrier is outdated or insufficient electricity grids, with around 2,500 gigawatts of power projects worldwide awaiting grid connection, highlighting the need for grid expansion and modernization.

body.label: Financing clean energy
body.text: High upfront costs and borrowing expenses limit clean energy adoption in developing countries, necessitating affordable capital and international financial support.

sections.heading: What were the main energy transition discussions at COP31?

body.label: Climate justice compact
body.text: UN Secretary-General António Guterres proposed a compact to support developing countries in transitioning from fossil fuels while protecting vulnerable populations through finance, adaptation, and cooperation.

body.label: Polluter pays principle
body.text: Guterres urged taxing fossil fuel companies’ windfall profits to fund climate action, noting the disparity between their earnings and funds available for vulnerable nations.

body.label: Methane emission reduction
body.text: Methane, a potent greenhouse gas, was highlighted as a climate emergency brake, with calls for near-zero methane emission standards and better leak detection.

body.label: Unresolved issues
body.text: Negotiations continue on climate finance predictability, loss and damage funding, emissions cuts, and mechanisms for a just transition protecting workers and communities.

sections.heading: Why is climate justice a key focus at COP31?

body.label: India’s energy efficiency efforts
body.text: India’s Bureau of Energy Efficiency organized a webinar during BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week 2026, promoting energy conservation, standards for appliances, and demand-side management to support sustainable consumption.

body.label: Global leadership attendance
body.text: While leaders like Turkey’s President Erdoğan and Brazil’s Lula da Silva attended, some major emitters such as the US and China sent lower-level representatives or were absent, affecting summit dynamics.

body.label: Brazil’s national roadmap
body.text: Brazil committed to developing national plans to reduce fossil fuel dependence and deforestation, building on COP30 outcomes.

sections.heading: How did India and other countries participate in COP31?

back2basics.text: The creamy layer refers to the relatively wealthier and better-educated members of Other Backward Classes (OBCs) who are excluded from reservation benefits to ensure affirmative action reaches the genuinely disadvantaged. Income and wealth criteria are used to identify this layer, and government orders specify which incomes count for this purpose.

2026-11-11-pm-9402aa9482.deck: The Supreme Court reaffirmed that parental salary and agricultural income should be excluded from the income test for determining OBC creamy layer status. This clarification affects reservation eligibility and has implications for social justice and constitutional law.

back2basics.text: GDP growth forecasts estimate the expected increase in a country’s economic output over a fiscal year. They are based on factors like consumption, investment, government spending, and external trade. These forecasts guide policymakers and investors by indicating economic health and potential challenges.

2026-11-11-pm-a2cf685054.deck: Moody’s has revised India’s GDP growth forecast for fiscal year 2026-27 to 7% due to broad-based economic momentum and resilience to energy supply shocks. This forecast is important for UPSC aspirants as it reflects India’s macroeconomic health and influences policy and development discussions.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about Moody’s FY27 GDP growth forecast for India:
1. Moody’s raised India’s GDP growth forecast to 7% due to broad-based economic momentum and energy supply shock resilience.
2. The forecast assumes no impact from inflation or monsoon variability on growth.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because Moody’s forecast acknowledges risks from inflation pressures and deficient monsoon affecting growth.

body.label: Broad-based economic momentum
body.text: Moody’s attributes the upward revision to robust consumption, improving investment dynamics, and strong macroeconomic fundamentals.

body.label: Energy supply shock resilience
body.text: India’s ability to diversify crude and gas supplies and buffer consumers through state-backed oil marketing companies and tax cuts helped it adjust better to energy price shocks.

body.label: Manufacturing and export strength
body.text: India’s large refining capacity limits fuel supply disruptions and supports its role as a major exporter of refined petroleum products.

body.label: Private investment prospects
body.text: High frequency indicators like capital goods production, industrial credit growth, and capacity utilisation suggest a new private capital expenditure cycle may be starting.

sections.heading: What are the reasons behind Moody’s upward revision of India’s FY27 GDP growth forecast?

body.label: Inflation pressures
body.text: Household consumption remains vulnerable due to intensifying price pressures with inflation near the upper end of the RBI’s 2-6% target range.

body.label: Agricultural output concerns
body.text: A deficient southwest monsoon and strengthening El Nino conditions are expected to weigh on agricultural output and rural demand.

body.label: Monetary policy impact
body.text: Further rate hikes by the RBI could delay recovery in private investment, potentially slowing growth.

back2basics.text: Monetary policy is the process by which a central bank controls money supply and interest rates to achieve economic objectives like controlling inflation and supporting growth. Liquidity management involves the central bank injecting or absorbing money in the banking system through tools like repo and reverse repo operations to maintain stability in short-term interest rates and ensure adequate cash flow in the economy.

2026-11-11-pm-b2dd94c4c6.deck: The Reserve Bank of India published detailed data on money market operations for November 9 and 10, 2026, showing volumes, rates, and liquidity injections. This data is crucial for understanding RBI's monetary policy stance and liquidity management, relevant for both Prelims and Mains preparation.

structure.intro: RBI uses money market operations as key tools to regulate liquidity and influence interest rates in the economy.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about RBI's money market operations in November 2026:
1. On November 9, 2026, RBI absorbed net liquidity of ₹1,48,423 crore through its operations.
2. The cash balances of scheduled commercial banks with RBI on November 10, 2026, were below the average daily cash reserve requirement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because the cash balances with RBI on November 10, 2026, were ₹8,47,268.91 crore, which is above the average daily cash reserve requirement of ₹8,16,655 crore.

body.label: Overnight segment
body.text: Includes call money, triparty repo, market repo, and repo in corporate bonds, with volumes and weighted average rates indicating short-term liquidity conditions.

body.label: Term segment
body.text: Covers notice money, term money, triparty repo, market repo, and repo in corporate bonds for longer tenors, showing medium-term liquidity trends.

body.label: Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) and related tools
body.text: RBI uses repo, reverse repo, Marginal Standing Facility (MSF), and Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) operations to inject or absorb liquidity daily.

body.label: Standing Liquidity Facility (SLF)
body.text: A refinance facility availed by banks from RBI to manage liquidity mismatches.

sections.heading: What are the key components of RBI's money market operations?

body.label: Liquidity injection and absorption
body.text: On November 9, RBI's net liquidity injection was negative ₹1,48,423 crore, indicating liquidity absorption; on November 10, it was negative ₹1,99,902 crore, showing increased absorption.

body.label: Outstanding operations impact
body.text: Outstanding operations on November 10 showed a net liquidity injection of ₹59,908.87 crore, partially offsetting the day's absorption.

body.label: Cash reserve position
body.text: Scheduled commercial banks held cash balances with RBI of ₹8,47,567.50 crore on November 9 and ₹8,47,268.91 crore on November 10, above the average daily cash reserve requirement.

sections.heading: How did RBI manage liquidity on November 9 and 10, 2026?

body.text: The data reflects how RBI implements monetary policy by managing liquidity and influencing short-term interest rates, crucial for understanding inflation control.

body.label: Financial governance relevance
body.text: Understanding RBI's liquidity operations helps analyze the central bank's role in financial stability and economic growth.

body.label: Prelims and Mains linkage
body.text: Questions on monetary policy tools, liquidity management, and their impact on the economy can be framed from this data.
